parole.testo: From Vulgar Latin *cāvicula, from Latin clāvicula (“pin”); probably via Old Occitan cavilla. Cognate with Italian caviglia, Portuguese cavilha, Occitan cavilha. Doublet of llavija, lavija, clavija, and clavícula. First attested in 1489.

From Vulgar Latin *iuxtāre, from Latin iuxtā (“near, beside”). Probably arrived through the intermediate of Old Occitan jostar (and later influenced by justo) or Catalan justar.
